section: Outbreak and spread - Mangal Pandey, Meerut; centres and leaders of the revolt
subsections: Revolt in Andhra and Hyderabad → leaders and places

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (Leader)
a. Dandasena
b. Korukonda Subba Reddy
c. Turrebaz Khan
 d. Mubariz-ud-Daula

List-II (Place or event)
i. Imprisoned in Golconda Fort
ii. Rebellion at Errannagudem
iii. Attack on the British Residency
iv. Rising at Paralakimidi

Codes:
accepted.x: Dandasena rose at Paralakimidi, Korukonda Subba Reddy led the rebellion at Errannagudem, Turrebaz Khan attacked the British Residency, and Mubariz-ud-Daula was imprisoned in Golconda Fort.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure leader–place pairs and eliminate codes containing a swapped association.
accepted.sec: Revolt in Andhra and Hyderabad → leaders and places

accepted.s: Dandasena, the Savara chief associated with the Revolt of 1857, rose at Paralakimidi after which development?
o: The ban on selling forest produce
The removal of the Nizam from Hyderabad
accepted.x: Dandasena rose at Paralakimidi on 9 August 1857 after the ban on selling forest produce.
accepted.tq: Link the local leader with the immediate cause rather than with a nearby Hyderabad event.
accepted.sec: Revolt in Andhra and Hyderabad → leaders and places

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Dandasena is correct?
o: He remained loyal to the Nizam and suppressed the uprising at Paralakimidi.
He was put down by Captain Wilson and was subsequently hanged.
He led the rebellion at Errannagudem and was imprisoned in Golconda Fort.
He attacked the British Residency at Hyderabad and escaped to Nepal.
accepted.x: Dandasena’s rising was suppressed by Captain Wilson, and Dandasena was hanged.
accepted.tq: Use the person–action–fate chain to reject swapped deeds and outcomes.
accepted.sec: Revolt in Andhra and Hyderabad → leaders and places

accepted.s:
Consider the following events:
1. Imprisonment of Mubariz-ud-Daula in Golconda Fort
2. Attack on the British Residency by Turrebaz Khan
Which of the following is the correct chronological order?
accepted.x: Mubariz-ud-Daula’s imprisonment in Golconda preceded Turrebaz Khan’s attack on the British Residency.
accepted.tq: Use the known before–after relationship to fix the sequence.
accepted.sec: Revolt in Andhra and Hyderabad → leaders and places

accepted.s:
With reference to the role of Hyderabad in the Revolt of 1857, consider the following statements:
1. Afzal-ud-Daula, the Nizam, remained pro-British.
2. The Nizam’s loyalty helped keep the Deccan quiet.
3. Andhra remained unaffected because it had no local leaders.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Afzal-ud-Daula remained pro-British, and the Nizam’s loyalty helped keep the Deccan quiet. Statement 3 is false because local risings occurred under Dandasena, Korukonda Subba Reddy and Turrebaz Khan.
accepted.tq: Find the absolute explanation in statement 3 and test it against the named local leaders.
accepted.sec: Revolt in Andhra and Hyderabad → leaders and places

accepted.s: The two principal local risings in Andhra associated with the Revolt of 1857 occurred at which pair of places?
accepted.x: Dandasena led the rising at Paralakimidi, while Korukonda Subba Reddy led the rebellion at Errannagudem; both occurred in August 1857.
accepted.tq: Separate the Andhra centres from the better-known northern and Hyderabad centres.
accepted.sec: Revolt in Andhra and Hyderabad → leaders and places

accepted.s: Who among the following was the correspondent of The Times who reported on the Revolt of 1857 and British reprisals?
accepted.x: W. H. Russell, correspondent of The Times, reported on the revolt and British reprisals in My Diary in India.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the contemporary reporter from political advisers and military officers.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: W. H. Russell — My Diary in India
Azimullah Khan — British commander at Paralakimidi
Captain Wilson — Adviser to Nana Saheb in London
accepted.x: W. H. Russell recorded his observations in My Diary in India. Azimullah Khan was Nana Saheb’s adviser, Captain Wilson suppressed Dandasena’s rising, and Mubariz-ud-Daula was imprisoned in Golconda Fort.
accepted.tq: Check whether the person is matched with his actual role, work or event.

accepted.s: Azimullah Khan went to London primarily to plead which case?
o: The restoration of the Nizam’s authority
The pension case of Nana Saheb
The forest-produce rights of Savara chiefs
accepted.x: Azimullah Khan, Nana Saheb’s adviser, went to London to plead Nana Saheb’s pension case.
accepted.tq: Connect the adviser with the specific political mission he undertook.

accepted.s: The Revolt of 1857 is regarded as the first great direct threat to British rule in India mainly because it
o: immediately resulted in the establishment of an independent Indian government
was confined exclusively to the urban elite
challenged British authority across several important centres and entered popular memory
was led entirely by the British-trained civil service
accepted.x: The revolt constituted the first great direct threat to British rule. Its heroes entered folklore and were later invoked during the Quit India and INA phases.
accepted.tq: Apply the historical significance to the broader political impact rather than to its immediate result.

accepted.s: The heroes of the Revolt of 1857 were later invoked particularly during which phases of India’s freedom struggle?
o: The Quit India and INA phases
The Swadeshi and Home Rule phases בלבד
The Non-Cooperation and Civil Disobedience phases בלבד
accepted.x: The heroes of 1857 entered folklore and were invoked during the Quit India and Indian National Army phases.
accepted.tq: Use the later historical association to distinguish the relevant freedom-movement phases.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the causes of the failure of the Revolt of 1857:
1. It lacked coordination and central leadership.
2. It did not have a common programme and adequate resources.
3. It had a narrow territorial and social base.
4. Urban elites and big princes generally stayed away.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The revolt suffered from lack of coordination, central leadership, a programme and resources. Its territorial and social base was limited, while urban elites and big princes generally remained aloof.
accepted.tq: Treat the four statements as complementary weaknesses and identify the comprehensive combination.

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT a major limitation of the Revolt of 1857?
o: Absence of a common programme and adequate resources
Participation of all major princes and urban elites
Lack of coordination and central leadership
accepted.x: Participation by all major princes and urban elites was not a limitation because many big princes and urban elites stayed away from the revolt. The other three were genuine weaknesses.
accepted.tq: Find the reversed comparison or participation claim among the genuine limitations.

accepted.s: The later use of the Hindu-Muslim unity displayed during the Revolt of 1857 was significant because it was cited against the
accepted.x: The Hindu-Muslim unity associated with the revolt was later cited against the two-nation theory.
accepted.tq: Match the historical experience with the later political theory it was used to challenge.

accepted.s: Which of the following was a major constitutional consequence of the Revolt of 1857?
o: The Act restored the authority of the East India Company over the Indian administration.
The Government of India Act, 1858 transferred power to the Crown.
The Act abolished the office of Governor-General and created only provincial governments.
The Government of India Act, 1858 transferred power to the elected Indian legislature.
accepted.x: The Government of India Act, 1858 transferred the governance of India from the East India Company to the British Crown.
accepted.tq: Identify the constitutional consequence while rejecting reversals of the transfer of power.

accepted.s: Who was the last major leader of the Revolt of 1857 to be executed?
accepted.x: Tantia Tope is regarded as the last major leader of the Revolt of 1857 to be executed.
accepted.tq: Use the LAST marker to distinguish the final major execution from other prominent leaders.
